string.text: Barman
Dead Channel: the Barman wants to talk.
Not now. I'll come back later.
Grek
A mercenary lieutenant at the Dead City base. Buys and sells whatever turns a profit, and remembers who owes him.
Lis
A courier the whole of Rostok buried three weeks ago. Very much alive.
Lis's PDA
A scratched courier's PDA, found among the wrecks of the Truck Cemetery. It is still sending the same looped signal.
Mercenary orders
Orders from a dead mercenary courier: an exchange at the railway depot in the Wild Territory. The seller signs himself "L."
Sealed crate
A sealed military crate with data disks: coordinates of army caches from before the second disaster. Ammunition, parts, medical supplies. Worth a fortune to the right buyer.
Barman here, from the 100 Rads. You're in Rostok - good. I have a job for someone who knows how to keep his mouth shut. Come to the bar.
Barman here, from the 100 Rads. Drop by when you're off duty - I have a job, and I'd rather your commanders didn't hear about it. Come to the bar.
Noted in the PDA: another lead on Lis.
Two leads point the same way: Lis went towards the Truck Cemetery. Time to follow the signal.
Barman here. My technicians went through that PDA, and I don't like what they found. Come to the bar.
The shooting has drawn attention: something is coming out of the depot's shadows. Snorks.
Grek's men take the crate. A transfer arrives on your PDA: Grek pays what he promised.
Lis is dead. If the crate was with him, it still is - and his hired guns won't let anyone take it quietly.
Lis and his men have stopped running - and they've turned their guns on you.
Grek's mercenaries arrive at the depot - and they've come for the crate, not to talk.
Grek's mercenaries arrive at the depot. They're with you: Lis and his men are the target.
Barman here. Word travels fast in the Zone - I hear the depot got loud. Come and tell me yourself.
Dead Channel

The crate is back in the Barman's hands. Lis bought his way out of the Zone with the Barman's own disks - for now. The caches from the disks are marked on your PDA. The story "Dead Channel" is complete.
The crate is back in the Barman's hands. Lis never made it out of the depot. The caches from the disks are marked on your PDA. The story "Dead Channel" is complete.
Lis got his way out of the Zone, and you got your share. The Barman will never know the whole story. The story "Dead Channel" is complete.
The crate went to the Dead City, Lis stayed at the depot for good, and the Barman lost his disks. The story "Dead Channel" is complete.
Dead Channel: The Signal
The Barman of the 100 Rads called me over the radio. He has a job for someone discreet. I should talk to him.
Dead Channel: Asking Around

Lis, the Barman's courier, vanished three weeks ago on the way back with a sealed crate. I should ask around Rostok: the Duty patrol at the gate, the guide, the Duty medic. Two good leads should be enough.
Dead Channel: Scrap and Radiation

The signal comes from the Truck Cemetery. I need to find Lis's PDA among the wrecks. Bandits have heard about the courier's "treasure" too - they'll come for anyone who gets close to it. Antirad will come in handy.
I have Lis's PDA. I should take it to the Barman.
Dead Channel: Guests in the Dead City
According to the PDA, mercenaries took the crate to the Dead City. A lieutenant called Grek should know more. I need to find him at the mercenaries' base.

According to the PDA, mercenaries took the crate to the Dead City - and the mercenaries won't talk to me. One of their couriers lies dead outside the base. Whatever he carried may tell me where the crate went.
Dead Channel: Exchange on the Tracks
The seller of the crate is Lis himself. The exchange is at the railway depot in the Wild Territory. I should talk to him before anyone starts shooting.
Lis gave up the crate and told his men to stand down. Grek's mercenaries came for it anyway - I need to get out of this alive, with the crate.
Lis and I split the deal. Grek's mercenaries are coming for the crate, with orders to take it off Lis's corpse - we hit them first. Lis and his men are on my side.
I sided with Grek's men. Lis and his guards have to die, and the crate is on Lis - I need to take it from his body.
Lis died before we could talk. The crate must be with him, and his men won't let me take it quietly.
Lis wouldn't give up the crate for free and is making a run for it with his men. I need to stop him.
Lis ran with the crate, and now he and his men are shooting back. The crate is on Lis - I need to take it from him.
The shooting has drawn snorks out of the dark. I need to deal with them.
Dead Channel: Reckoning
Whatever happened at the depot, the Barman is waiting for an answer. I should go back to the 100 Rads.
You called, Barman?

I did. Three weeks ago I paid for a run. Lis - a courier, a reliable one - was to bring me a sealed crate from a former army man. Disks, with coordinates of army caches from before the second disaster: ammunition, parts, medicine. Lis never came back. Somewhere around the Truck Cemetery he vanished, and we all drank to his memory.
And now?

Now my radio picks up his PDA every night. The same looped signal: static, a scrap of his voice, coordinates. I don't want Duty in on this - Voronin would take the disks before I said a word. I need someone from outside. I'll pay an advance. Ask around first, quietly: somebody must have seen him before he left.

Now my radio picks up his PDA every night. The same looped signal: static, a scrap of his voice, coordinates. You wear the Duty patch, I know - but I've seen you, you're a man of your word. If Voronin hears of those disks, he'll take them before I say a word. So this stays between us. I'll pay an advance. Ask around first, quietly: somebody must have seen him before he left.
I'll find out what happened to Lis.
Here's the advance, and something against the radiation - you'll need it out there. Talk to the Duty patrol at the gate, to the guide, and to the Duty medic. Somebody saw something.
Don't take too long. A signal like that draws more than just me.
Do you remember a courier called Lis? He left about three weeks ago.
Lis? I remember. He went out through this gate at dawn, towards the Truck Cemetery.
Anything unusual about him?
His backpack. Heavy as a sack of cement - he could barely walk straight. For a man going to pick something up, he was carrying a lot.
Lis, sure. Strange one, that. Before he left he went round the whole bar and paid off every debt he had. To the last coupon.
Why is that strange?
Because he hadn't been paid yet - the money was to come when he got back. Who settles his debts before a job, unless he isn't planning to come back?
Lis... he bought from me just before he left. Antirad, bandages, a lot of both.
How much is a lot?
Enough for a week out there, not a day trip. I asked him if he was moving out. He laughed.
I found Lis's PDA at the Truck Cemetery. The bandits were all over the place.
Let me see... The last entry: "Ambush. Mercenaries. They took the crate. Heading for the Dead City." So that's how it ended.
So Lis is dead?
Maybe. Something about this smells, though. I'll give the PDA to my technicians, let them go through everything on it. Here's your pay for now. Come back in an hour or so - I'll call you.
You called. What did the technicians find?

That last entry - about the mercenaries - was written after the signal started. After Lis was supposed to be dead. Somebody went back to that PDA. Either the mercenaries are playing with me, or Lis is. Go to the Dead City and find out where my crate is. Their lieutenant, Grek, handles their deals.
I'll pay the Dead City a visit.
Careful there. Mercenaries smile right up to the moment they shoot.
Don't wait too long. Crates like that don't stay in one place.
I'm here about a crate. Sealed, with disks inside. It belongs to the Barman.
Belongs? We didn't take it in any ambush, friend. We bought it. Half paid; the seller wants the rest at the exchange. And the seller is a courier called Lis - alive and well, if you're wondering.
That crate was stolen from the Barman.
Need an extra gun at the exchange?
I'll think about it.
Stolen, bought - the Zone doesn't care. But I'm not greedy. Fifteen thousand and my boys stay home. Lis can wait at the depot for buyers who never come.
Deal. Here's the money.
That's too much.

Pleasure doing business. The exchange is at the railway depot in the Wild Territory. Lis will be there with the crate and his two hired guns - and nobody from us. What you do with him is your business.
Then come back when you've found the money. Or don't.

Security, eh? Fine. My squad goes to the railway depot in the Wild Territory - meet them there. You watch Lis's hands, they bring the money, you get a cut. Lis isn't the trusting kind, and neither am I.
Think fast. The exchange won't wait.
Lis. Everyone in Rostok thinks you're dead.
That was the idea. The PDA, the signal, the entry about the ambush - all so nobody would come looking. Should have smashed the thing instead. So, who sent you? The Barman?
Why did you do it?

Because the Barman would have paid me pennies for disks worth a fortune. Twelve years I've carried other people's crates through this place. One chance to get out of the Zone for good - that's all I wanted. So, what now?
The Barman gets his crate. Hand it over.
Forget the Barman. We split it - half for me.
Sorry, Lis. Grek pays better.
Pleasure. Here's the crate. Boys, lower your guns - we're done. And a word of advice: Grek's men are on their way for that box. If you want to keep it, get ready.
Pleasure. Here's the crate. Boys, lower your guns - we're done here. Tell the Barman whatever you like.
Just like that? I'm not dying for that box - but I'm not giving it away either. Five thousand, and it's yours. Call it my ticket out of the Zone.
Deal. Five thousand.
No deal. That crate isn't yours to sell.
Then you'll have to take it from me. Boys - we're leaving!

Half... fine, deal. But listen: Grek's men will be here any minute. They bring money for half the crate and orders to take the rest off my corpse - I know how Grek does business. So we hit them first, and we keep their money and the crate. Here's your advance. Get to cover.

Half... fine. Nobody's coming anyway - you paid Grek to stay home, didn't you? Then it's done: here's your share of what he paid me up front. I'll sell the disks far away from Rostok. Watch the shadows on your way out - the depot isn't empty at dusk.
You son of a... Boys, he's with them!
Here's your crate. Lis is alive - he sold it back to me and ran.
Sold it back... with my own disks. Well, at least it's back where it belongs. He'll show his face in Rostok one day, and we'll talk then.
And the disks?

Some of them are mine now, some are yours - I'm not ungrateful. Here's your pay and a few things from my storeroom. And I've copied some of the coordinates to your PDA. Go and get those caches before somebody else does.

Some of them are mine now, some are yours - and not a word to Voronin, we agreed. Here's your pay and a few things from my storeroom. And I've copied some of the coordinates to your PDA. Go and get those caches before somebody else does.
Here's your crate. Lis didn't make it.
Didn't make it... I wanted to look him in the eye, here, in front of everyone. Well. The crate is what I paid for.
And my pay?
Here. Less than for the whole job - a man who stole from me should have answered for it in this bar, not died in the mud. A couple of the cache coordinates are on your PDA. Go and get them.
Lis is gone. The crate too.
Gone... Well. At least now we know he isn't sending signals from the other side. Thanks for trying, stalker.

Gone, is he? Funny - a man who paid off every debt and stocked up for a week before a one-day run. And now he's gone, and you come back with nothing. I'll remember this, stalker. Now drink your vodka and go.
The crate went to the mercenaries.
To the mercenaries. With your help, I'd bet. Then you've nothing more to do in my bar - not on this business. Get out.
